Phase 71 implemented per the approved plan (docs/phases/cockpit-rules-tab.md @ a7ee220) at c6bab73, branch phase-71-cockpit-rules-tab. gate: see entry.

What changed, where:
- tagteam/cockpit_api.py: rules_payload(). Enforced rows come from gatekeeper.resolve_gatekeeper / panel.resolve_panel / briefer.resolve_briefer / config.resolve_watcher / cycle.STALE_ROUND_LIMIT, one builder per row, each wrapped so one failure never hides the others. The prose follows the resolved spec, `applies` is on every row, and the test command never appears. stop.{effective, source, project, run, run_mode_roadmap, project_shadowed_by, has_run_override, effective_text, shadow_note}. watcher_stale_config comes from read_beat().started_at against tagteam.yaml's mtime, gated on beat_view (per your r2 note). ORDER_PRESETS, project_orders_ok. _plan("orders") maps onto orders_command argv: one line, ≤500 chars, --by web user.
- tagteam/config.py resolve_watcher(); tagteam/watcher.py _watch_locked now calls it (same default-on-problem behaviour).
- tagteam/orders.py: orders_command(out=) so the cockpit can capture its output. CLI unchanged.
- tagteam/server.py: GET /api/rules and POST /api/orders (cockpit mode only; legacy mode gives 404; POST needs the token).
- cockpit.html / .css / .js: a Rules tab and a banner-delimited "Phase 71" slice that only presents the payload.
- docs: how-tagteam-works (the Rules tab, `orders …` in the CLI-equivalence line); roadmap Phase 71b entry (tagteam.yaml edits, depends on 71).

Verification:
- tests/test_cockpit_rules.py, 31 tests. Criterion 8: invalid gate → OFF; unknown watcher key → 15 = the watcher's own resolve; missing lens brief → panel OFF; no provider → briefer OFF; an invalid block beside a valid one; gate prose for on_submit/impl-only/no-tests/scope-off; command never shown. Criterion 9 (a)–(d) through the API. Criterion 10 with heartbeat fixtures. Read-only, creates nothing. _plan mapping and bad params. The real server (dry_run writes nothing, token required, 409 on refusal, cockpit-only). The shipped slice in REAL Chromium: groups apart by computed border style (solid/dashed) plus markers, saved value per scope, radio back to saved until the write lands, every post body, locked project editing, no overflow.
- Mutation check: switching the gate row to the raw getter fails 2 tests.
- Focused runs: server_cockpit, cockpit_activity, watcher, config, orders, cockpit_rules, readonly, docs_story: 512 passed.
- Hand check in a real page (the phase doc lists screenshots and what they found). Criterion 9 (a)–(d) were driven by clicks, with `tagteam orders` agreeing after each write, plus the stale-watcher notice and 390 px. Looking at the page found and fixed three things (uncaptioned/stretched scope toggles; a malformed orders file inviting refused edits → project_orders_ok locks project editing; the stop shown twice).

Deviation: the tab is tested in real Chromium instead of the node stub, which can't see computed style, checked/disabled or overflow.
Only table-tested: panel ON / briefer ON as rendered rows.

GATE: PASS | scope 11 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2385 passed, 5 skipped, 7m58s)
checked: HEAD c6bab73

Reviewed c6bab73 against the approved Phase 71 plan. REQUEST_CHANGES:

1. [P2] Preserve the advisory draft and focus across refreshes (tagteam/data/web/cockpit.js:757-788; refreshAll at 1058). renderAdvisory clears rules-add and creates a fresh empty input every time /api/rules returns. The new refreshAll hook runs on SSE changes and the existing 30-second live tick (and polling fallback), so typing an unfinished note loses both its text and focus without any user action. Changing the note scope also destroys the draft, and ordersAct reloads even after a refused write. Reproduced with the shipped slice in real Chromium: renderRules(PAYLOAD), enter and focus an unfinished note, renderRules(PAYLOAD) again => value is empty and focused is false. Preserve draft text, focus/selection and chosen scope during refresh; clear the submitted draft only after its successful add. Add browser coverage for background refresh and failed/cancelled submission.

2. [P2] Surface panel/briefer validation problems even when enabled is malformed (tagteam/cockpit_api.py:_panel_row and _briefer_row, around 1591 and 1615). Both rows suppress all resolver problems unless the raw enabled field is exactly True. Thus panel: invalid, panel.enabled: "true", and the equivalent briefer configurations show an ordinary off row with warnings=[] although their runtime resolver explicitly reports a malformed mapping/boolean. This violates the approved resolver-problems-to-warnings behavior and hides why the intended rule cannot run. Preserve actual validation problems independently of the raw enable flag, keeping absent/valid disabled blocks quiet. Cover malformed mappings and enable values alongside a valid independent row.

3. [P2] Reject invalid scope and removal-ID types before building CLI argv (tagteam/cockpit_api.py:_plan_orders). run is True silently treats every non-boolean value as project scope, while int(id) truncates fractional IDs and accepts booleans. In an isolated project I confirmed {op: stop, value: roadmap, run: "true"} succeeds and saves the PROJECT stop; after adding note #1, {op: remove, id: 1.9} succeeds and deletes #1. These bad params should give 400 without mutation, as the plan promises, rather than selecting another scope or note. Validate an explicitly supplied run as a boolean and id as an actual integer (integer strings may remain accepted); reject fractional and boolean IDs. Exercise the real endpoint, including unchanged files/state on rejection.

Verification: accepted the recorded gate PASS at c6bab73 (2385 passed, 5 skipped); did not rerun the full suite. Focused tests/test_cockpit_rules.py: 31 passed. Additional deterministic real-Chromium draft reproduction and isolated-project resolver/action reproductions above. Inspected the submitted narrow Rules screenshot. No arbiter interjections or advisory standing orders were present.

All three r1 findings are fixed at the new HEAD (see the gate entry for the commit). gate: see entry.

1. [P2] The draft survives refreshes. The unfinished note lives in RULES.draft, updated on `input`. renderAdvisory captures focus and selection from the old input before rebuilding and restores both, and a scope change keeps the text. ordersAct takes an onOk that runs only when r.ok, so the draft is cleared only when its own add succeeds (and only if the draft still equals the submitted text). A refused write reloads with the draft intact, and a cancelled confirm never reaches onDone. Real-Chromium test test_a_draft_survives_refreshes_and_is_cleared_only_by_its_own_success covers: a background re-render keeps value, focus and caret [4,6]; a scope change; a refused submit; a cancel; success clears the draft. Removing the restore line fails it.

2. [P2] Panel and briefer warnings are keyed on the block being PRESENT (`"panel" in config` / `"briefer" in config`), not on enabled being exactly True. So `panel: invalid`, `panel.enabled: "true"`, `briefer: invalid` and `briefer.enabled: "yes"` each show their resolver problems, beside a valid watcher row (7 min). An absent block, and a valid `enabled: false` block, stay quiet (warnings == []). Both are parametrized tests.

3. [P2] Strict params. A supplied non-null `run` must be a real bool, so "true" and 1 give a 400. `id` must be an int (not a bool) or a digit string, so 1.9, True and "-1" give a 400. The real-endpoint test posts {stop roadmap, run:"true"}, {remove id:1.9} and {remove id:true}: each is a 400, and tagteam-orders.json and handoff-state.json are byte-identical afterwards. The _plan table also has the new bad cases.

Mutation check: disabling the run check plus the panel presence rule fails 6 tests. Focused: test_cockpit_rules (45) + test_server_cockpit: 73 passed.

GATE: PASS | scope 11 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2399 passed, 5 skipped, 7m57s)
checked: HEAD 33ae377

Approved at 33ae377. Reviewed the revision against all three round-1 findings and the approved Phase 71 plan.

The advisory draft is now retained independently of the rebuilt input; refresh restores focus/selection, and the success callback clears only the matching submitted draft. Refused writes and cancelled confirmations retain it. Panel/briefer rows expose resolver problems for present malformed blocks while absent/valid disabled blocks remain quiet. Scope and removal-ID validation rejects the previously demonstrated wrong-scope and truncated-ID writes before dispatch; endpoint regressions verify 400 responses and unchanged orders/state bytes.

Verification: 73 passed in the focused tests/test_cockpit_rules.py and tests/test_server_cockpit.py run, including the real-Chromium draft regression. Accepted the recorded gate PASS at the submitted HEAD 33ae377 (2399 passed, 5 skipped; scope and plan-doc passed); did not rerun the full suite. No remaining blocking findings. No arbiter interjections or advisory standing orders were present.
